entries.text: `vector_search` declares its embedding columns with an explicit 4-byte element type on every engine (`REAL[n]` on DuckDB and the generic default, `ARRAY<REAL>` for Spark, Databricks, Doris, StarRocks, LakeSail, PySpark and Velox), matching the float32 data it generates. Engines that read the old `FLOAT` as double precision now store `REAL`: DuckDB (`DOUBLE[n]` to `REAL[n]`), Spark and Databricks (`ARRAY<DOUBLE>` to `ARRAY<FLOAT>`), Doris (`ARRAY<DOUBLE>` to `ARRAY<FLOAT>`), Trino (`ARRAY(DOUBLE)` to `ARRAY(REAL)`) and Redshift (`DOUBLE PRECISION` to `REAL`). Top-k ids are identical, but `vector_search` load and query timings change on those six engines, so do not compare them with earlier runs. PostgreSQL, Snowflake, ClickHouse, SingleStore, StarRocks and BigQuery keep their column types. A guard test rejects bare `FLOAT` in benchmark schema specs, the Snowflake FlightData type map writes `DOUBLE` instead of `FLOAT` (the same 64-bit type), and the StarRocks and SingleStore adapters no longer pass `float_as_real` because no benchmark schema declares a bare `FLOAT`.
